title: On the stability of learning
why_read: A theoretical paper on when noisy, infrequent learning signals make training unstable, relevant mainly to computational neuroscience and biologically-inspired learning researchers.
analysis: The paper shows that if gradient-like learning signals arrive sparsely and noisily, as they might in real neurons, a learning process can have unbounded variance even when it converges correctly on average. This formalizes a subtlety distinct from standard stochastic gradient descent stability analysis, adding a constraint for models of biologically plausible learning. It's a mathematically rigorous but narrow contribution, useful chiefly to people modeling learning in brains or designing sparse-feedback training schemes rather than mainstream ML engineers.
